events.title: Ageing Badly
events.description: ‘Ageing Badly’ challenges assumptions that the goal of one’s later years is to age well or ‘successfully’, a message that, since the 1960s, has become pervasive, naturalised in medicine, social theory, and popular culture. Ageing badly, by contrast, encompasses a range of uncomfortable and idiosyncratic ways in which art works, bodies, artists, and ideas, such as ‘the 1960s’, have aged over time. The language of ageing is deeply entangled with those concerning time, history, and the body—languages that have in turn shaped the field of art history and feminist interventions in the field.

events.title: Who persists into computing (and why)
events.description: As computing becomes central to how neuroscience is done, computational thinking is quickly becoming an essential part of training for the next generation of neuroscientists. At the same time, there are longstanding gender and racial inequities in computer science — without addressing these, we run the risk of propagating the same inequities when we bring computing into neuroscience. Our recent mixed methods work in a large sample of students and professionals demonstrates that there continue to be gender disparities in who considers themselves a programmer and who persists into computing.
